_disclaimer: SIMULATED DEMONSTRATION QUESTIONS. These are illustrative triage prompts, not a validated screening instrument, and no clinician has reviewed them. Costs are rough estimates of effort, not measured times.
_design_note: Every question names the confidence driver it addresses, who can answer it, and what each answer does to the patient record. The answer effects are field assignments applied by core/questions.py; a question that cannot state what its answers would change is a question we cannot compute a value for, and is therefore not in this file.
_cost_note: cost_seconds is effort, not clock time -- it is what the question costs the person asking. Retrieving a record or phoning a relative is expensive because it occupies a nurse, not because the seconds matter. Cost is a tie-breaker in ranking and never a reason to skip a question that can move a band; see the ranking policy below.
_ranking_note: Band movement dominates deliberately. A question that raises confidence without being able to change what we do about the patient is tidying, not triage. Cost can demote a question by at most max_cost_penalty, so an expensive question that can move a band still outranks a free one that cannot.
_direction_note: deescalation_only_weight prices a question whose answers can only propose a LOWER band. Because of the ratchet such a question cannot move a waiting patient at all; its value is that it hands a nurse documented grounds for a review they would otherwise have no basis for. Real, and worth a fraction of finding somebody sicker than we thought. Ranking the two equally would let the questioner spend its one cheap question confirming that a patient is fine.
_asking_policy_note: A cap exists because the failure mode of an adaptive questioner is an interrogation. A patient in pain being asked eleven questions by a screen is a worse experience than being asked none, and the marginal question is almost always worth less than the one before it.

questions.text: Is this facial asymmetry new today, or has your face always looked this way?
Did the headache come on suddenly, and is this the worst you have ever had?
You have told us you are not short of breath. Can you walk across the room, or say a full sentence without stopping?
Any pain, pressure or tightness in the chest, jaw or arm?
Retrieve prior records: conditions, regular medications, previous attendances.
Take a fresh set of observations.
On a scale of nought to ten, how bad is the pain right now?
Ask the parent: is the baby feeding normally, and are the nappies as wet as usual?
Are you taking any blood thinners, or anything for your heart or blood pressure?

answers.label: yes, a heart or blood pressure tablet

questions.text: Did you hit your head, and did you black out at any point?
